test.name: Walking skeleton through the CLI and GUI

expected: Instances created, started, and stopped through stackly show up in the Stackly window without a refresh, survive closing and quitting the app and a killed or stopped stacklyd with the same PID, never appear twice, and leave no fake process after stop
steps: on the commit this record was made on, with a clean tree: `cargo build -p stacklyd -p stackly-cli -p stackly-fake-server`, `cargo build -p stacklyd --example skeleton_seed`, and `cargo xtask build-app` (Debug app at target/xcode/Build/Products/Debug/Stackly.app); in Terminal A `export R="$(mktemp -d /tmp/stk-skel.XXXXXX)"` and `S=target/debug/stackly`
seed: `target/debug/examples/skeleton_seed --root "$R"`; note the runtime UUID on the `runtime` line as RT

Terminal B: `STACKLY_ROOT="$R" target/debug/stacklyd` and leave it running (stacklyd reports `degraded` in `stackly daemon status` because no catalog is found outside an app bundle; that is expected here)

Terminal C: open the app on the same root with `STACKLY_ROOT="$R" target/xcode/Build/Products/Debug/Stackly.app/Contents/MacOS/Stackly`, select Instances, and expect the footer `stacklyd running` and the page `No Instances`

Terminal A: `STACKLY_ROOT="$R" $S instance create demo --runtime $RT --provider testing/fake --revision 0.2.0 --set-json readyDelayMs=3000 --wait`; expect, without clicking or refreshing anything, a row `demo` whose second line names the fake provider and runtime version 0.1.0, status Stopped; copy the instance UUID from the last output line as ID

`STACKLY_ROOT="$R" $S instance start $ID --wait` (takes about 3 s); expect the row to show a starting status first, then Running and ready, with no click; `STACKLY_ROOT="$R" $S instance get $ID` shows `Lifecycle running`, `Readiness ready`, and `Process pid <PID>`; write PID down; `ps -axww -o pid=,args= | grep "$R" | grep "stackly-fake-server serve" | grep -v grep` shows exactly one line with that PID

close the Stackly window with the red button: the notice `Stackly is still running` appears; the same `ps` line and `instance get $ID` (`running`, same PID) are unchanged; click Stackly in the Dock and expect the window back with the same `demo` row, Running
press ⌘Q; `instance get $ID` still shows `running` with the same PID; start the app again as in step 4 and expect the `demo` row Running without a refresh

Terminal B: Ctrl+C on stacklyd; expect the banner `Can’t connect to stacklyd.` with the time and the `demo` row kept; the fake `ps` line is still there with the same PID; run `STACKLY_ROOT="$R" target/debug/stacklyd` again; expect the banner gone within a few seconds and `instance get $ID` showing the same PID with `adopted` on the Process line

Terminal A: `kill -9 $(pgrep -f "target/debug/stacklyd")` (check with `pgrep -fl stacklyd` that it names only this daemon), then start stacklyd again in Terminal B; expect the same as the previous step: the same PID, `adopted`, exactly one fake `serve` process in `ps`, and exactly one `demo` row in the window

failed init: `STACKLY_ROOT="$R" $S instance create broken --runtime $RT --provider testing/fake --revision 0.2.0 --set-json failInit=true --wait`; expect exit 7, `code: supervisor.init_failed`, state `needs_recovery`, and a row `broken` shown as Failed (write down the operation UUID as OP1); then `STACKLY_ROOT="$R" $S operation abandon $OP1 --yes`, which prints `abandoned operation ... (state failed)` and one `secret_ref` leftover with `compensation_failed`; write down whether the `broken` row is still in the window afterwards

interrupted create: `STACKLY_ROOT="$R" $S instance create slow --runtime $RT --provider testing/fake --revision 0.2.0 --set-json initDelayMs=20000` without `--wait`; as soon as `ps -axww -o pid=,args= | grep "$R" | grep -v grep | grep "stackly-fake-server init"` shows a line (within a second or two), `kill -9` stacklyd and start it again; expect a single `slow` row shown as Failed (never two), `STACKLY_ROOT="$R" $S operation inspect <op>` with `State needs_recovery`, and, within 20 s of the create, the `init` helper gone from `ps` on its own; then `operation abandon <op> --yes`

stop: `STACKLY_ROOT="$R" $S instance stop $ID --wait`; expect the `demo` row to become Stopped without a click, `instance get $ID` `Lifecycle stopped` with `Process -`, and `ps -axww -o pid=,args= | grep "$R" | grep stackly-fake-server | grep -v grep` printing nothing

clean up: Ctrl+C stacklyd in Terminal B, ⌘Q the app, `ps -axww -o pid=,args= | grep -E "stackly|$R" | grep -v grep` shows nothing from this run, then `rm -rf "$R"` and unset R; also remove the leftover folder `ls -d "$TMPDIR"stackly-*` that stacklyd made for the socket if one stays after a kill -9 (check with `ls "$TMPDIR" | grep '^stackly-'`)

fill in this record: steps (note any change), actual (what you saw at each numbered step, the PID, and the `broken` row result), status (PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED with reason and owner), reviewer, and finishedAt, then run `cargo xtask evidence check`
